REAL ESTATE DEEP MASTER CORPUS — 1,850 EXAMPLES
=================================================

Expanded from the supplied real-estate curriculum from foundational property
concepts through professional finance, valuation, law, development, urban
economics, private equity, capital markets, REITs, PropTech and integrated
case studies.

EXACT TOTAL: 1,850 EXAMPLES.

All financial numbers are illustrative educational assumptions and are not
investment recommendations. Actual transactions require jurisdiction-specific
legal, tax, zoning, title, lending, appraisal, environmental, insurance and
regulatory analysis.

Every sample follows:
CONCEPT → ILLUSTRATIVE NUMBERS → FORMULA → CODE/SPREADSHEET PATTERN →
CASE STUDY → DUE DILIGENCE → RISK → SCENARIO ANALYSIS → DECISION QUESTIONS.

EXAMPLE 0001 | Foundations & Property | buzzer control
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CONCEPT
-------
Analyze buzzer control as part of foundations & property, linking the legal, physical,
market, operational and financial characteristics of real property.

ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO
---------------------
Asset type: office repositioning
Units: 27
Purchase price: $1,817,000
Monthly rent/unit: $937
Gross potential rent: $303,588
Vacancy: 4.0%
Effective gross income: $291,444
NOI: $190,896
Entry cap rate: 10.51%
Illustrative loan: $1,017,520
Interest rate: 5.25%
Annual debt service: $80,070
DSCR: 2.38x

FORMULA / MODEL
---------------
Cap Rate = NOI / Value = 10.51%

CODE / SPREADSHEET PATTERN
---------------------------
```python
purchase_price = 1817000.00
units = 27
monthly_rent = 937.00
vacancy = 0.040
opex_ratio = 0.345

gpr = units * monthly_rent * 12
egi = gpr * (1 - vacancy)
noi = egi * (1 - opex_ratio)
cap_rate = noi / purchase_price

print({"gpr": gpr, "egi": egi, "noi": noi,
       "cap_rate": cap_rate})
```

CASE STUDY
----------
For office repositioning, the analyst first identifies the investment objective and
submarket. The analyst verifies ownership, permitted use, physical condition,
leases, historical operations, comparable properties, financing terms and
capital requirements. A complete decision then compares the base case with
downside and upside cases instead of relying on a single return metric.

DUE DILIGENCE
-------------
• title and ownership
• survey and site measurements
• zoning and permitted use
• building condition
• environmental conditions
• rent roll and lease abstracts
• historical income and expenses
• taxes and insurance
• capital expenditure needs
• financing and lender covenants
• market supply and demand
• exit liquidity

RISK TEST
---------
Primary stress case: vacancy rises during lease rollover.
Secondary stress case: exit capitalization rates expand.

Also test rent growth, vacancy, expense growth, leverage, interest rate,
capital expenditure, exit cap rate and hold period.

ADVANCED ANALYSIS
-----------------
Create BASE / DOWNSIDE / UPSIDE scenarios and compare NOI, DSCR,
cash-on-cash return, unlevered IRR, levered IRR, NPV and equity multiple.
Identify which assumption produces the greatest change in value.

DECISION QUESTIONS
------------------
1. What is the highest and best use?
2. What evidence supports revenue assumptions?
3. Which assumptions require independent verification?
4. What causes permanent loss of capital?
5. What happens if refinancing is unavailable?
6. What happens if the exit cap expands?
7. Which legal, physical or market risk dominates?
8. What is the appropriate exit strategy?

CROSS-DISCIPLINARY LINK
-----------------------
Connect buzzer control to law, finance, valuation, development, urban economics,
operations, taxation, GIS/PropTech, sustainability or risk management.

• exit liquidity

---------

capital expenditure, exit cap rate and hold period.

CONCEPT
-------
Analyze DNS as part of real estate law & land rights, linking the legal, physical,
market, operational and financial characteristics of real property.

ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO
---------------------
Asset type: land development
Units: 39
Purchase price: $41,309,000
Monthly rent/unit: $2,149
Gross potential rent: $1,005,732
Vacancy: 8.0%
Effective gross income: $925,273
NOI: $536,659
Entry cap rate: 1.30%
Illustrative loan: $24,785,400
Interest rate: 6.00%
Annual debt service: $2,031,633
DSCR: 0.26x

FORMULA / MODEL
---------------
Equity Multiple = Total Distributions / Total Equity Invested.

CODE / SPREADSHEET PATTERN
---------------------------
```python
purchase_price = 41309000.00
units = 39
monthly_rent = 2149.00
vacancy = 0.080
opex_ratio = 0.420

gpr = units * monthly_rent * 12
egi = gpr * (1 - vacancy)
noi = egi * (1 - opex_ratio)
cap_rate = noi / purchase_price

print({"gpr": gpr, "egi": egi, "noi": noi,
       "cap_rate": cap_rate})
```

CASE STUDY
----------
For land development, the analyst first identifies the investment objective and
submarket. The analyst verifies ownership, permitted use, physical condition,
leases, historical operations, comparable properties, financing terms and
capital requirements. A complete decision then compares the base case with
downside and upside cases instead of relying on a single return metric.

DUE DILIGENCE
-------------
• title and ownership
• survey and site measurements
• zoning and permitted use
• building condition
• environmental conditions
• rent roll and lease abstracts
• historical income and expenses
• taxes and insurance
• capital expenditure needs
• financing and lender covenants
• market supply and demand
• exit liquidity

RISK TEST
---------
Primary stress case: title, zoning or environmental problems emerge.
Secondary stress case: market rent is below the underwriting assumption.

Also test rent growth, vacancy, expense growth, leverage, interest rate,
capital expenditure, exit cap rate and hold period.

ADVANCED ANALYSIS
-----------------
Create BASE / DOWNSIDE / UPSIDE scenarios and compare NOI, DSCR,
cash-on-cash return, unlevered IRR, levered IRR, NPV and equity multiple.
Identify which assumption produces the greatest change in value.

DECISION QUESTIONS
------------------
1. What is the highest and best use?
2. What evidence supports revenue assumptions?
3. Which assumptions require independent verification?
4. What causes permanent loss of capital?
5. What happens if refinancing is unavailable?
6. What happens if the exit cap expands?
7. Which legal, physical or market risk dominates?
8. What is the appropriate exit strategy?

CROSS-DISCIPLINARY LINK
-----------------------
Connect DNS to law, finance, valuation, development, urban economics,
operations, taxation, GIS/PropTech, sustainability or risk management.

---------------------------
```python
purchase_price = 30449000.00

opex_ratio = 0.420

egi = gpr * (1 - vacancy)
noi = egi * (1 - opex_ratio)
cap_rate = noi / purchase_price

       "cap_rate": cap_rate})
```

• exit liquidity

• exit liquidity

• exit liquidity

---------

• exit liquidity

---------

capital expenditure, exit cap rate and hold period.

-----------------

Analyze Python MQTT service as part of advanced integrated case studies, linking the legal, physical,

ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIO
---------------------
Asset type: multifamily acquisition
Units: 350
Purchase price: $5,610,000
Monthly rent/unit: $1,110
Gross potential rent: $4,662,000
Vacancy: 9.0%
Effective gross income: $4,242,420
NOI: $2,566,664
Entry cap rate: 45.75%
Illustrative loan: $3,422,100
Interest rate: 7.50%
Annual debt service: $307,827
DSCR: 8.34x

FORMULA / MODEL
---------------
NPV = discounted future cash flows − initial equity.

CODE / SPREADSHEET PATTERN
---------------------------
```python
purchase_price = 5610000.00
units = 350
monthly_rent = 1110.00
vacancy = 0.090
opex_ratio = 0.395

gpr = units * monthly_rent * 12
egi = gpr * (1 - vacancy)
noi = egi * (1 - opex_ratio)
cap_rate = noi / purchase_price

print({"gpr": gpr, "egi": egi, "noi": noi,
       "cap_rate": cap_rate})
```

CASE STUDY
----------
For multifamily acquisition, the analyst first identifies the investment objective and
submarket. The analyst verifies ownership, permitted use, physical condition,
leases, historical operations, comparable properties, financing terms and
capital requirements. A complete decision then compares the base case with
downside and upside cases instead of relying on a single return metric.

-------------
• title and ownership
• survey and site measurements
• zoning and permitted use
• building condition
• environmental conditions
• rent roll and lease abstracts
• historical income and expenses
• taxes and insurance
• capital expenditure needs
• financing and lender covenants
• market supply and demand
• exit liquidity

RISK TEST
---------
Primary stress case: market rent is below the underwriting assumption.
Secondary stress case: financing becomes more expensive.

Also test rent growth, vacancy, expense growth, leverage, interest rate,
capital expenditure, exit cap rate and hold period.

ADVANCED ANALYSIS
-----------------
Create BASE / DOWNSIDE / UPSIDE scenarios and compare NOI, DSCR,
cash-on-cash return, unlevered IRR, levered IRR, NPV and equity multiple.
Identify which assumption produces the greatest change in value.

DECISION QUESTIONS
------------------
1. What is the highest and best use?
2. What evidence supports revenue assumptions?
3. Which assumptions require independent verification?
4. What causes permanent loss of capital?
5. What happens if refinancing is unavailable?
6. What happens if the exit cap expands?
7. Which legal, physical or market risk dominates?
8. What is the appropriate exit strategy?

Interest rate: 5.25%
Annual debt service: $585,869
DSCR: 11.28x

FORMULA / MODEL
---------------
Cap Rate = NOI / Value = 56.80%

CODE / SPREADSHEET PATTERN
---------------------------
```python
purchase_price = 11633000.00
units = 483
monthly_rent = 1813.00
vacancy = 0.040
opex_ratio = 0.345

gpr = units * monthly_rent * 12
egi = gpr * (1 - vacancy)
noi = egi * (1 - opex_ratio)
cap_rate = noi / purchase_price

print({"gpr": gpr, "egi": egi, "noi": noi,
       "cap_rate": cap_rate})
```

CASE STUDY
----------
For affordable-housing project, the analyst first identifies the investment objective and
submarket. The analyst verifies ownership, permitted use, physical condition,
leases, historical operations, comparable properties, financing terms and
capital requirements. A complete decision then compares the base case with
downside and upside cases instead of relying on a single return metric.

DUE DILIGENCE
-------------
• title and ownership
• survey and site measurements
• zoning and permitted use
• building condition
• environmental conditions
• rent roll and lease abstracts
• historical income and expenses
• taxes and insurance
• capital expenditure needs
• financing and lender covenants
• market supply and demand
• exit liquidity

RISK TEST
---------
Primary stress case: insurance becomes expensive or unavailable.
Secondary stress case: operating expenses increase faster than rent.

Also test rent growth, vacancy, expense growth, leverage, interest rate,
capital expenditure, exit cap rate and hold period.

ADVANCED ANALYSIS
-----------------
Create BASE / DOWNSIDE / UPSIDE scenarios and compare NOI, DSCR,
cash-on-cash return, unlevered IRR, levered IRR, NPV and equity multiple.
Identify which assumption produces the greatest change in value.

DECISION QUESTIONS
------------------
1. What is the highest and best use?
2. What evidence supports revenue assumptions?
3. Which assumptions require independent verification?
4. What causes permanent loss of capital?
5. What happens if refinancing is unavailable?
6. What happens if the exit cap expands?
7. Which legal, physical or market risk dominates?
8. What is the appropriate exit strategy?
